payload.description:
Assistant messages where the content field is a plain string (not a list of content blocks) are silently dropped during ingestion.

Evidence: Session d473cc02-1874-43f5-81e0-761a9691af0c has 1884 records in the database, but an assistant message at timestamp 2026-03-16T07:30:31 is missing. The message exists in the JSONL file (confirmed via grep) with plain text content: "No. Kind can't bind the same ports twice..."

payload.title: Ingestion does not capture 100% of JSONL session lines in DuckDB
payload.description:
GOAL: every line of every ~/.claude JSONL transcript must become exactly one row in the records table (one row per line, append-only, idempotent, content-faithful). Current ingest_jsonl()/_extract_blobs() in core.py violate this in three ways found during review:

1. MISSING-UUID PK COLLAPSE (silent data loss). core.py:365 uses record.get('uuid', '') and uuid is the records PRIMARY KEY. Every line lacking a uuid maps to the empty-string key; with INSERT OR IGNORE only the FIRST uuid-less record per DB survives and all subsequent uuid-less lines are silently dropped. Fix: synthesize a stable surrogate key for uuid-less lines (e.g. sessionId + line hash or sessionId+offset) instead of '' so each line gets a distinct PK.

2. BLOB OFFLOADING IS UNRECOVERABLE (content not actually in DuckDB). Server always ingests with blob_root set (server.py:147,174). _extract_blobs (core.py:233-297) strips any content block >100KB (BLOB_THRESHOLD_BYTES, blobs.py:24) and replaces it with a '[Large Content: file_id]' marker; the real content goes to the on-disk blob store. read_blob() (blobs.py:67) has ZERO callers, so offloaded content is unreachable through any query/context/summarize path. Net effect: large lines are NOT captured in the queryable store. Fix: either wire read_blob() into the query/context paths to rehydrate, or expose blob content via SQL (e.g. a view/table) so 100% of content is reachable.

3. MALFORMED-LINE + RE-SERIALIZATION CAVEATS. core.py:355 silently skips lines that fail json.loads (acceptable but should be counted/surfaced, not dropped invisibly). Separately, when blob_root is set core.py:361 does line = json.dumps(record) so records.raw is a re-encoded copy, not the original bytes (key order/whitespace/unicode-escaping differ) even for lines with no blob. Verify this is acceptable; if byte-faithfulness is required, store the original line.

Related already-fixed boundary bugs in this same path (is-b3b dropped records under concurrent write/read; is-a2a refresh returning processed:0 for appended lines) show this is the highest-risk area for the 100%-capture invariant. Add a regression test asserting line-count(file) == row-count(records) for a session containing uuid-less lines and >100KB content blocks.

payload.description:
## Gap

ingest-sessions has no first-class way to retrieve a FULL session by session_id. Today only:

- `context(session_id)` returns the LCM summary-DAG recovery context (a SUMMARY, not the full session).
- `query(sql)` is manual SQL over `records`; you can `SELECT raw FROM records WHERE session_id=? ORDER BY timestamp`, but large content blocks are offloaded to a blob store (`[Large Content: file_...]`, rehydrated via `read_blob(file_id)`), so full reconstruction is clunky and easy to get wrong.

There is no get-full-session primitive: context=summary, query=SQL-with-blob-offload.

## Desired

A tool/endpoint, e.g. `get_session(session_id, {include_blobs=true, format})`, that returns the full transcript reassembled in chronological order with all `[Large Content: file_...]` markers rehydrated via read_blob, optionally paginated/streamed for large sessions, and a stable citation form (so a labbook `session_id` resolves to the actual content).

## Use case

Durable cross-repo citation. labbook/ADR entries now reference sessions by id (e.g. mtm `docs/labbook/2026-06-22-verification-is-ast-decidable-or-observational-not-semantic.md`) as the canonical, durable reference of record — the mtm labbook now treats ingest-sessions as the session reference of record, not the filesystem. An amnesiac agent must be able to retrieve the cited session's full content on demand from just the id.

## Acceptance

Given a known `session_id`, the tool returns the complete ordered transcript with blobs rehydrated; round-trips a session whose content exceeds the inline blob threshold.
payload.title: Add first-class full-session retrieval by session_id (ordered records + blob rehydration)

payload.description:
## Why
Agents are anterograde-amnesiac: durable RECORD is solved (sessions are stored here; curated findings live in consuming repos as labbook/ADR), but RECALL is not — nothing surfaces relevant prior reasoning into a fresh session BY CONSTRUCTION. ingest-sessions should become the on-device retrieval BRAIN; a thin Claude Code UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart hook injects whatever it returns (hook stdout / hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is injected as context — Claude Code hooks docs https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).

## Corpus decision: ALL sessions, not just curated derivatives
Curation is the unreliable step (the amnesiac can't be trusted to distill), so restricting retrieval to curated docs caps recall at the distilled fraction. The raw sessions are PRIMARY SOURCE, not lossy auto-summaries — retrieve over them. BUT raw sessions contain dead ends, errors, and later-REVERSED conclusions, so retrieval MUST be supersession/confidence-aware or it surfaces overturned reasoning as settled (is-X.2).

## Architecture (the seam — keep this repo project-AGNOSTIC)
- BRAIN here: corpus + embedding/BM25 index + cross-encoder rerank + supersession/confidence graph + retrieval API. On-device (latency: the per-prompt hook is synchronous, sub-second budget) and reused cross-repo via MCP.
- Thin adapters OUTSIDE (per consuming repo, e.g. mtm): (a) artifact->supersession-link adapter mapping that repo's git reverts / issue-tracker closes / ADR amendments into the GENERAL supersession-link form this repo ingests; (b) the harness hook that calls the retrieval API and formats injection. Do NOT hardcode any consumer's tracker/ADR semantics here.

## Children
- is-X.1 retrieve_relevant API (two-stage retrieve -> cross-encoder rerank, on-device).
- is-X.2 supersession + confidence + trust-tier ranking (the hard part / differentiator).
- Existing is-6f5 (get_full_session by id) is the on-demand FETCH primitive of this same surface — reframe as member of the retrieval API family.

## Prior art (this is a known pattern; reuse, don't reinvent the retrieval stack)
- ClawMem (yoloshii) — on-device hooks+MCP, hybrid RAG: BM25 + vector + RRF + query expansion + cross-encoder rerank + composite scoring (recency decay, confidence, content-type half-lives): https://github.com/yoloshii/ClawMem
- mann1x/claude-hooks — Qdrant + memory KG, HyDE, attention decay, 'deterministic memory recall': https://github.com/mann1x/claude-hooks
- claude-mnemonic (lukaszraczylo): https://github.com/lukaszraczylo/claude-mnemonic ; claude-mem (auto-capture + inject) https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture
- 'Storage Is Solved, Injection Isn't' (the gap is relevance/injection): https://alexandrekhoury.com/writing/superbrain-session-memory-claude-code
- Hindsight is 20/20 — agent memory retain/recall/reflect (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.12818
THE GAP none of them close: explicit SUPERSESSION linking + primary-source-vs-auto-summary TRUST-TIERING. They retrieve auto-extracted summaries flatly; we rank raw primary source with supersession awareness. That is the novel work (is-X.2).

payload.description:
First-class retrieval API alongside context()/query(). Stage 1: BM25 + vector candidate retrieval (sqlite-vec + local embeddings, e.g. all-MiniLM-L6-v2) over records. Stage 2: cross-encoder rerank (e.g. cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) jointly scoring (query, candidate) -> relevance. PRETRAINED zero-shot — no project labels at cold start. On-device + sub-second (the per-prompt UserPromptSubmit hook is synchronous; remote calls blow the budget). Query = prompt + recent transcript/context. Returns ranked records + pointers + get_full_session ids (is-6f5) for on-demand deepening. Two stages are required over 9000+ sessions (don't rerank-all). Ranking policy is is-565's other child (supersession/confidence/trust-tier); this pebble is the retrieve+rerank pipeline. Parent: is-565.

Sources: ClawMem hybrid pipeline https://github.com/yoloshii/ClawMem ; cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 ; sqlite-vec + all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ; Claude Code hooks (injection target) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

Acceptance: given (query, context) returns top-k ranked records sub-second on-device; integrates get_full_session (is-6f5); pretrained reranker works with zero project training.

payload.description:
Rank candidates by relevance x recency-decay x confidence x NOT-superseded, so retrieval never surfaces an overturned or mid-flight-wrong statement as settled (raw sessions are full of dead ends, errors, reversals). Parent: is-565.

1. SUPERSESSION (novel; nobody does this): ingest 'record A supersedes record B' links in a GENERAL form, fed by per-consumer adapters that translate git reverts / issue-tracker closes / ADR amendments (those semantics stay OUT of this repo). Down-weight/flag superseded records; derive simple cases internally where observable.
2. CONFIDENCE + RECENCY decay (prior art): ClawMem composite scoring (recency decay, confidence, content-type half-lives) https://github.com/yoloshii/ClawMem ; mann1x/claude-hooks attention decay https://github.com/mann1x/claude-hooks .
3. TRUST-TIER: weight raw PRIMARY-SOURCE records above the LCM auto-summary tier (sprigs/bindles); an auto-summary must never outrank a contradicting primary-source record. This repo already has both tiers — this is ranking over them.

GAP these tools leave: flat retrieval of auto-extracted summaries with decay but NO explicit supersession-linking and NO primary-vs-summary trust-tier. That is this pebble.

Acceptance: for a query where a plan was chosen then later removed (build-then-revert arc), the superseding conclusion outranks/flags the reversed one; the auto-summary tier never outranks a contradicting primary-source record.

After the one-time full backfill (99.97%, 869968/870236), the in-server backfill uses keyset-from-max(uuid). Since session uuids are random (uuid4), records ingested AFTER the cursor passed their uuid range are never picked up by a keyset-from-max re-run -> coverage silently decays as new sessions arrive (the ~268 current stragglers are this effect).

Also wire a periodic FTS rebuild (record_fts is a snapshot; new records aren't searchable lexically until rebuilt). Parent: is-565.

DISCOVERED in prod 2026-06-23 at ~873k records. core.rebuild_fts_index does, ON THE SINGLE DB THREAD: SELECT all ~873k raw, DELETE record_fts, recompute json.loads(raw)+record_text for every row (Python, one thread), executemany INSERT, then PRAGMA create_fts_index. This blocks ALL queries (every _db_execute) for ~45 MINUTES. The periodic sync (is-565.5) calls it whenever embedded>0, so any trickle of new sessions re-triggers a 45-min service-wide stall every cycle. MITIGATION IN PLACE: systemd drop-in sets INGEST_SESSIONS_SYNC_INTERVAL=86400 (~/.config/systemd/user/ingest-sessions.service.d/override.conf) to effectively disable the periodic sweep; remove it once fixed.

Also NON-ATOMIC: a restart during the rebuild left record_fts partial (90,053 of 873,713 rows) while the fts_main_record_fts index snapshot is from the prior full build -> inconsistent lexical state (vector arm unaffected; retrieve_relevant still works, lexical recall degraded).

FIX:
1. Build the new (uuid,text) projection OFF the DB thread (json.loads+record_text in asyncio.to_thread, chunked); do only the DB writes + create_fts_index on the DB thread, ideally as a single atomic transaction (build shadow table -> swap) so an interrupt rolls back cleanly.
2. Decouple FTS-rebuild cadence from every embed: throttle (e.g. at most every N hours, or only when record count grew by >X%), since DuckDB FTS is snapshot-only (no incremental).
3. After the fix, run ONE clean full rebuild to repair the current partial record_fts.
Parent: is-565 (regression from is-565.5 sync path).

payload.body: REFINEMENT (principal): version ordering only matters at PyPI publish (an index resolves 'latest'); a uv-tool-from-git install pins the exact ref, so the version is provenance-only. Don't hardcode 0.0.0 permanently — make the custom version source: if HEAD is on an exact tag (git describe --exact-match --tags) emit that tag (e.g. 0.2.0, the PyPI release version); ELSE emit 0.0.0+g<short-sha>. No .dev<N> distance, no semver guessing. Net: every dev/tool build is 0.0.0+g<sha>; publishing to PyPI is just 'git tag 0.2.0' on the release commit (the local +sha is dropped, PyPI gets a clean 0.2.0). Senior-SRE + FP review of the tools server.py exposes (query, get_session, retrieve_relevant, context, refresh, summarize, add_supersession, backfill, sync):

1) SECURITY DEFECT (headline, independently shippable, highest priority): the 'query' tool runs ARBITRARY SQL on a READ-WRITE DuckDB connection (server.py:737 duckdb.connect(path), no read_only). An agent-facing tool can DROP/DELETE/UPDATE/run DDL against the sessions corpus. FIX: the read path uses a read-only connection (duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True)); 'query' rejects non-SELECT + enforces a statement timeout + row/result cap. Separate the WRITER connection (ingest/backfill/sync/summarize) from the READER (query/retrieve/get_session/context) so a query tool cannot mutate BY CONSTRUCTION.

2) FOOTGUN: retrieve_relevant unconditionally runs the stage-2 cross-encoder (retrieval.py:381) with no cheap tier and no bounded budget, so it HANGS to the client timeout instead of fast-failing. The cheap stage-1 retrieve_candidates (no model) exists but is NOT exposed as a tool. FIX: a rerank opt-out returning stage-1 fused candidates; a bounded rerank budget that returns a clear signal rather than blocking; make the cheap/bounded op the convenient default, the cross-encoder opt-in (it is the hook-time top-k-into-context precision tier, not needed for agent lookups).

3) SEPARATION: read, heavy-compute, and mutating/admin tools are flat-mixed on one surface. Separate reads (read-only, bounded) from writes/admin (effectful, guarded, idempotent, concurrency-controlled — the _backfill_running guard is the right pattern; extend to every heavy op).

4) FAST-FAIL: no tool has a bounded execution budget at the MCP boundary; every blocking op (model load/inference, big session rehydrate, arbitrary SQL) hangs until the CLIENT times out with no informative response. Give each blocking tool a budget and fail fast + observably ('exceeded budget / too large / still running'), never a silent hang.

FP framing: the retrieval CORE is cleanly functional-core/imperative-shell, but the SERVER boundary inverts it — the default operation is the most expensive AND most dangerous. Make effects + costs explicit in each tool's type; default to the cheapest/safest/bounded op, expensive/effectful opt-in. Points: 8 (item 1 splittable + first).

payload.description:
REPRODUCED INCIDENT (2026-06-28 ~17:07). Two mcp__ingest-sessions__query calls timed out in a live parent session: (1) a LIKE '%...%' full scan over 'records'; (2) a TRIVIAL 'SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN (table,view)'. The trivial one timing out is the tell. retrieve_relevant had worked moments earlier (59KB result), so the server/embedding path was alive.

ROOT CAUSE (evidence-backed, run-before-read):
The server serializes ALL DB work onto ONE thread with ONE connection and ONE queue (server.py:7-10, _db_loop @ ~734, _db_execute @116 waits on req.done with NO timeout). Every tool's DB touch — including the trivial schema lookup — is FIFO-queued. The expensive LIKE full scan (over an 83GB DB) and/or a watchdog-triggered ingest of the parent's own actively-growing session JSONL occupied the DB thread; the trivial query queued BEHIND it and the MCP client timed out waiting. This is head-of-line blocking, NOT a slow schema lookup, NOT cross-process lock contention.

NOT lock contention: lsof shows ONLY the production server (PID 1608682, '6uW' write lock) holds the file. An external read_only open fails INSTANTLY (0.04s): 'IO Error: Could not set lock ... Conflicting lock is held in /usr/bin/python3.12 (PID 1608682)'. The two wedged 'timeout 10 uv run ingest-sessions-server --port 18741/18742' processes (etime ~17 days, from repos/ingest_sessions) do NOT hold this DB. So the stall is internal to the one server, not multi-process.

DB BLOAT (separate, compounding pathology):
- sessions.duckdb = 83G on disk (du), 188G apparent/sparse (ls). WAL tiny (61K-218K) and actively flushing (mtime tracks now) -> DB is operational, not a stale-journal/corruption case.
- blobs/ offload dir is only 652K -> blob offload barely used; large raw transcripts + FTS(BM25) index + HNSW embeddings live INLINE in the DB. DuckDB does not reclaim space on DELETE/UPDATE without a full CHECKPOINT/VACUUM rewrite; the FTS rebuild does DELETE+INSERT+create_fts_index (server.py ~396) which churns the file, so 4.5 days of incremental ingest + repeated FTS rebuilds grow it monotonically.
- Server RSS = 42.6 GB (ps rss 42642060 KB), NLWP 224. 'db = duckdb.connect(path)' (server.py:737) sets NO config: no memory_limit, no threads cap, no statement timeout. DuckDB then defaults memory_limit to ~80% of RAM -> the 42GB resident footprint.

HEALTH: Cannot run PRAGMA integrity_check externally — the server holds an exclusive RW lock (read_only open fails instantly, see above), and stopping the live server is out of scope for this diagnosis. Operational signals indicate a HEALTHY-but-bloated DB, not corruption: server up 4.5d, retrieve_relevant returns correct results, WAL small + flushing, no stale/giant -wal/-journal sidecar. Recommend an integrity_check during the next maintenance stop.

RELATION TO is-fd7: is-fd7 covers the MCP-surface design (read-only query connection, bounded/opt-out retrieve_relevant, read/write tool separation, per-tool fast-fail budgets) and its item 4 overlaps the fast-fail aspect here. But is-fd7 does NOT diagnose (a) that a TRIVIAL query times out due to single-DB-thread HOL queueing — a per-query budget alone does NOT fix this, because the trivial query never even starts until the blocking one finishes; the EXPENSIVE op must itself be bounded/interruptible to free the queue — nor (b) the 83GB/42GB memory+disk bloat. This bug is the concrete reproduced incident + those two new items.

SUGGESTED FIX:
1. Bound the EXPENSIVE op on the DB thread, not just the waiter: enforce a DuckDB statement timeout (SET statement_timeout / Connection.interrupt() on budget) so a runaway LIKE scan is killed and the queue drains — this is what actually unblocks the trivial query (complements is-fd7 item 4, does not duplicate it).
2. Set explicit connect config: duckdb.connect(path, config={'memory_limit': '<bounded>', 'threads': <cap>}) to stop the 42GB RSS growth.
3. Address disk bloat: periodic CHECKPOINT + a maintenance VACUUM/rewrite (DuckDB: copy to a fresh file) to reclaim FTS DELETE+INSERT churn; and/or actually use the blobs offload for large raw transcripts (currently 652K used vs 83GB inline).
4. Give _db_execute a bounded wait so the server returns an explicit 'busy/over-budget' rather than relying on the client timeout (the silent-hang in _db_execute @116).
5. Reap the wedged repos/ingest_sessions :18741/:18742 'timeout 10' servers (env hygiene; not the cause but stale).

EVIDENCE COMMANDS: ls -lh + du -h on ~/.local/share/ingest_sessions/sessions.duckdb*; lsof/fuser on the DB; ps -o rss,nlwp,etimes -p 1608682; read_only duckdb.connect -> instant lock conflict; grep of server.py:737 connect (no config) and _db_loop single-thread queue.

payload.body: CORRECTION to the initial diagnosis (subagent over-reached on 'bloat'): 83GB is SMALL for DuckDB — NOT bloated; drop the VACUUM/CHECKPOINT recommendation. Indexes are NOT missing for indexed columns: create_tables (core.py:198) issues CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS for records(session_id|type|timestamp), the record_fts FTS index, and HNSW on record_embeddings/summary_embeddings; the INSTALLED server (~/.local/share/uv/tools/ingest-sessions/.../core.py) contains all of them; committed since 2026-03-06 (git blame); and _db_loop runs create_tables on EVERY startup (server.py:739). Actual root cause of the observed timeouts: (1) the raw query() tool let a caller run a leading-wildcard 'text LIKE %..%' — un-indexable by btree (only the FTS index/match_bm25 serves text search; LIKE bypasses it) → full scan of records.text; (2) that scan monopolized the SINGLE DB thread/connection (server.py:733 _db_loop, one FIFO queue), so a trivial follow-up query queued behind it; (3) _db_execute waits with NO statement_timeout, so the client timed out. retrieve_relevant is unaffected because it uses FTS+HNSW, not LIKE. FIX (revised): add a DuckDB statement_timeout / Connection.interrupt() to bound any single op on the DB thread so it can't starve the queue; route text search in the query path through the FTS index (match_bm25) rather than LIKE; OPTIONAL: a second read-only connection for catalog/trivial queries so they don't queue behind heavy scans. NOT a fix: VACUUM (no bloat) or adding btree indexes (already present; and they can't serve LIKE anyway). RESIDUAL: physical index presence in the live file is unconfirmed (server holds exclusive lock; read-only open refused) — verify with SELECT * FROM duckdb_indexes() at the next maintenance stop.

payload.description:
MOTIVATION: The MCP surface exposes an arbitrary-SQL tool (query(sql)) — that is the root design flaw, not just a tuning gap. It let a caller run a leading-wildcard 'text LIKE %..%' full scan over the 83GB records table, which (on the single-connection _db_loop) starved every other query (is-189). An interface that ALLOWS a poor-performing query is a bad interface: the connection pool (is-189) bounds the blast radius, but the real fix is to make slow queries UNREPRESENTABLE.

PREMISE: We already know the full set of query patterns we need against this data, even if today's ergonomics are off. So the open-ended SQL surface buys nothing and costs correctness.

SCOPE (review THEN propose — design deliverable, not necessarily the full impl in this pebble):
1. INVENTORY every consumer of ingest-sessions: the MCP tools (query, retrieve_relevant, get_session, context, summarize, query/sync/refresh/backfill, add_supersession, etc.), the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact hooks, ranking.py/retrieval.py callers, and any external/agent callers. For each, record the ACTUAL access pattern it needs.

SCOPE ADD (per principal): do NOT just inventory current programmatic consumers — MINE PAST SESSIONS for every actual raw-SQL/query() use and WHY it was needed, so the bounded interface is driven by real historical demand. Evidence gathered (retrieve_relevant over session history) — the raw-SQL usage collapses to a small recurring set, and the SAME failures repeat every time:

1. SCHEMA RE-DISCOVERY EVERY TIME (dominant waste): sessions repeatedly run 'SELECT name FROM sqlite_master' then 'information_schema.columns' to learn table/column names, and STILL guess wrong ('wrong column names, wrong table names', 'didn't match the schema', expecting id/project/created_at when it is session_id/project_path/modified). Evidence: sessions ee52eb5d, 20a1f97e, 0b5908a4, 552de17d, 414453f2, 71332b3b, cea64cd5. A typed interface ELIMINATES this entire class.

2. LEXICAL CONTENT SEARCH WITH STRUCTURED FILTERS (the real workhorse): 'raw ILIKE %oracle%', 'summaries.content LIKE %coverage%', scoped by project_path LIKE %mtm%/%biscayne%/%aspergillus%, by git_branch, EXCLUDING tool_result noise ('raw NOT ILIKE %tool_result%'), ranked by count(*) hits GROUP BY session_id. Evidence: 6262da9e (oracle hunt), ee52eb5d/20a1f97e (coverage/playwright/spa), 552de17d (multilang-support), 9... This is exactly the un-indexable leading-wildcard LIKE that starves the DB thread (is-189) — and exactly what a first-class FTS-backed search(text, project, branch, role, exclude_tool_results, group_by_session, limit) should serve via match_bm25 + indexed filters.

3. PROJECT/BRANCH/TIME SCOPING: filter sessions by project_path/git_branch/recency — needs indexed columns + a typed filter, not LIKE on project_path.

4. GET-BY-ID + COUNT/RANK: fetch a session's records (get_session covers this), count hits per session, top-N by hits.

5. THIS SESSION'S need (another data point): I used raw SQL to find a specific USER DIRECTIVE by exact content ('config repo-specific'); retrieve_relevant (semantic rerank) BURIED it because it ranks by similarity, not exact phrase. So a LEXICAL exact/substring search filtered by role=human/origin is a distinct, needed capability that semantic retrieve_relevant does NOT cover.

CONCLUSION for the design: the closed set is overwhelmingly (a) FTS-backed lexical search with structured filters (project/branch/role/type, exclude tool_result) + per-session hit-count ranking, (b) project/branch/time scoping, (c) get-by-id, (d) lexical-exact directive/phrase search (role=human) — and schema-discovery vanishes entirely under a typed API. Twin root failures to design out: schema-rediscovery-by-trial-and-error AND un-indexed leading-wildcard LIKE. The proposal must show each historical raw-SQL query above mapping onto a typed, index-backed method.

Current state: ingestion only reads Claude Code session JSONL from ~/.claude/projects (server.py _projects_dir/_ingest_all/_ingest_file_full/_ingest_jsonl, with _derive_session_metadata/_build_session_metadata), treating each line as a flat record and threading by file order. omp (Oh My Pi) sessions are not ingested.

Format differences a parser MUST handle (authority: omp://session.md, omp://session-operations-export-share-fork-resume.md):
- On-disk: ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<dir-encoded>/<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl; content-addressed blobs at ~/.omp/agent/blobs/<sha256>; subagent sub-sessions live beside the parent as <session>/<AgentId>.jsonl (recursive).

Branched omp sessions will mis-thread if ingested by line order. buildSessionContext semantics: compaction entries replace history from firstKeptEntryId; branch_summary/custom_message become synthetic messages.

- Content externalization: image blocks >=1KiB are stored as blob:sha256:<hash> refs (resolve from the blob store or record a marker); large strings truncated at 500000 chars with '[Session persistence truncated large content]'; transient fields partialJson/jsonlEvents are absent.

payload.description:
Production incident: the live DB (~/.local/share/ingest_sessions/sessions.duckdb) reached
861 GiB apparent (369 GB actual on ZFS) and the server process held ~84 GiB RAM + ~7 GiB
swap (100% of swap consumed). Two independent root causes.

## Root cause 1 — unbounded memory (immediate, fixable)

`_db_loop` in src/ingest_sessions/server.py does `db = duckdb.connect(path)` with NO
`memory_limit` and NO `threads`. DuckDB then defaults `memory_limit` to 80% of system RAM
(~150 GB on this host) and `threads` to core count (~225 threads observed). The buffer pool
grew to ~84 GB and pushed the machine into swap.

Fix (applied with this pebble): `SET memory_limit='32GB'` and `SET threads='8'` immediately
after connect.

## Root cause 2 — disk bloat from FTS rebuild churn (the big one, NOT fixed here)

`record_fts` held 256,032,432 storage rows but only 1,061,128 live rows — ~255 MILLION dead
tombstone rows. DuckDB FTS is snapshot-only: `core.write_fts_index` does a full
`DELETE FROM record_fts` + re-INSERT of ~1M rows + `create_fts_index(overwrite=1)` on EVERY
FTS refresh. ~240 refreshes over 11 days on a never-restarted server. DuckDB does not
reclaim deleted-row space in place, so every refresh permanently appends.

### Evidence (benchmarked on the live DB — do not re-test)
- `FORCE CHECKPOINT` on the live DB: 27.7s, reclaimed ZERO bytes.
- A per-cycle CHECKPOINT bounds growth for a plain DELETE+INSERT table, but NOT for an
  FTS-indexed one.
- `drop_fts_index` + recreate is no better than `create_fts_index(overwrite=1)` — both leak
  ~31 blocks per rebuild.
- DuckDB docs: VACUUM does not reclaim space; CHECKPOINT only partially merges adjacent
  row groups (~25% deletes) and does not shrink the file. The ONLY full compaction is
  `COPY FROM DATABASE` into a fresh file.
  https://duckdb.org/docs/current/operations_manual/footprint_of_duckdb/reclaiming_space
- Open upstream issue: "VACUUM FULL not implemented — no native way to reclaim space after
  deletes/drops". https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/21154

## Fix design

### IMMEDIATE (done in the commit referencing this pebble)
Cap the connection: `SET memory_limit='32GB'`, `SET threads='8'` in `_db_loop`. Bounds RAM;
does nothing for disk.

### SPACE (tracked here, NOT implemented)
The service must SELF-MANAGE compaction on its own db-thread. It owns the single writer, so
a cron job is the wrong shape — a cron would fight the service for the write lock. Design:
- Trigger on a bloat threshold: apparent size from `pragma_database_size` vs. live-row size.
- On trigger, during idle: `COPY FROM DATABASE` rebuild into a fresh file, rebuild the
  derived FTS/HNSW indexes, atomic swap.
- Independently, cut FTS-rebuild frequency — 240 rebuilds in 11 days is the actual driver of
  the bloat.

### STRATEGIC (tracked here, decision needed)
DuckDB structurally cannot serve a mutable long-lived server that needs space reclaim plus
incremental FTS. Three-way choice:
(a) Stay on DuckDB + self-managed periodic `COPY FROM DATABASE` + memory cap.
(b) SQLite: FTS5 is incremental, VACUUM is real, sqlite-vec for vectors; keeps the
    embedded/no-daemon property. Risks: sqlite-vec ANN maturity, row-store scan performance,
    SQL-dialect rewrite including the `query` MCP tool contract, extension-loading packaging.
(c) Postgres: autovacuum, incremental GIN FTS, pgvector, real concurrency — at the cost of
    running a server.

payload.description:
## Motivation
exophial wants to audit reducer runs by reading worker session transcripts (the structured superset of the reducer log's flattened worker-stdout dump). Today ingest_sessions is an MCP SERVER package: core deps are duckdb + fastembed (onnxruntime + a downloaded model) + mcp + starlette + uvicorn + watchdog. exophial importing the whole thing would (a) drag onnxruntime/uvicorn into exophial's 'self-contained pure-Python wheel' distribution, and (b) pull semantic-search/reranking machinery it does not need to audit ONE run.

## Desired state
Split the package so the TRANSCRIPT INGESTION + STRUCTURED QUERY CORE is an importable library with a LIGHT dependency floor, and the heavy layers are optional extras:
- core (importable by exophial): duckdb + the jsonl parsing/ingestion + per-run/per-session/per-record accessors. Returns structured records — tool_use inputs, tool_result outputs, per-message usage/cost, timestamps, uuid/parentUuid threading, sidechain records, final result. NO fastembed, NO uvicorn.
- [server] extra: mcp + starlette + uvicorn + watchdog (the MCP server, ingest-sessions-server).
- [embeddings]/[search] extra: fastembed (embeddings.py, rerank.py, semantic retrieval).

## Concretely
- pyproject: move fastembed/mcp/starlette/uvicorn/watchdog OUT of [project.dependencies] into optional-dependencies extras; core deps = duckdb (+ stdlib json). Guard imports so importing the core never imports fastembed/server modules.
- Expose a stable public API (e.g. ingest_sessions.reader / a documented core surface) that exophial pins against: ingest a set of session files -> structured rows; query a run's workers by session id.

## Relationship
- Complements is-5a7 (adds omp as a transcript SOURCE). Together: exophial gets a backend-agnostic, importable audit reader — Claude Code JSONL today, omp/anthropic sources as they land, all behind one reader API.
- Consumer side is an exophial pebble: import this lib, stop teeing worker stdout into dispatcher.log (#4 -> captures only), point run-audit at the transcript behind a per-backend transcript seam, plus a reducer-owned structured terminal-outcome event + an 'exophial audit' verb.

## Acceptance
- A fresh env installs ingest_sessions CORE (no fastembed/onnxruntime/uvicorn present) and imports the reader; it ingests a real Claude Code session .jsonl into structured rows (tool calls, usage/cost, threading) with duckdb only.
- The MCP server + semantic retrieval still work when the [server]/[embeddings] extras are installed (no regression).
- exophial can add ingest_sessions (core) as a dependency without onnxruntime/uvicorn entering its wheel.

The landed omp adapter requires the `session` header to be LINE 0. On the real
corpus it almost never is, so 307 of 323 omp files are silently classified
`claude` and ingested through the wrong parser.

Measured 2026-08-06 against ~/.omp/agent/sessions (323 *.jsonl on disk), using
the landed code:

  probe_session_format:  {'claude': 307, 'omp': 16}
  first-line type:       {'title': 307, 'session': 16}
  session-header index:  {0: 16, 1: 307}
  files with a session header in their first two lines: 323 / 323

A real file begins:

  line 0  {"type":"title","v":1,"title":"Pull from remote","source":"auto",
           "updatedAt":"...","pad":"                      ...   "}
  line 1  {"type":"session","version":3,"id":"019fa9bd-f2b3-7000-aa10-...",
           "cwd":"/home/rix/code/git_puller/repos/ingest_sessions",
           "title":"Pull from remote"}
  line 2  {"type":"model_change","id":"f3b29721","parentId":null,...}

The `title` line is a fixed-width, rewritten-in-place record (note its `pad`
field) that omp keeps at the head of the file so the title can be updated
without rewriting the whole transcript. It is a preamble line, not a
SessionEntry: it carries no `id` and no `parentId`, so it can never be a DAG
node.

A full-corpus rehearsal into a throwaway DuckDB (never the live one) confirms
the consequence: 323 omp paths recorded in file_mtimes but only 201 records
and 16 session rows, because only the 16 header-at-line-0 files reached the
omp adapter. The other 307 went down core.ingest_jsonl.

Change, in src/ingest_sessions/omp.py and whatever core.probe_session_format
needs to follow:

- Locate the session header by SCANNING the leading lines for the first
  object whose type == "session" with a non-empty id, instead of requiring
  index 0. Bound the scan to a small fixed number of leading lines (2 covers
  every file on disk today; keep the bound small so a Claude Code transcript
  is never re-classified as omp by a `session`-shaped line deep in the file).
- probe_session_format must use the SAME bounded scan, so classification and
  ingestion can never disagree about whether a file is omp.
- Every line at or before the header index is session-level PREAMBLE:
  consumed for metadata where it has any, never inserted as a record, never
  counted as malformed. The `title` preamble line's title is the same string
  the header already carries, so the header stays the metadata authority.
- Lines after the header index parse as the SessionEntry union exactly as
  they do today. Nothing about DAG threading, versioning, subagent handling
  or field mapping changes.

Acceptance, measured against a THROWAWAY DuckDB cold-scanned over the two real
default roots resolved from the invoking user's passwd entry
(pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir), never the live corpus and never $HOME
(the acceptance grader pins HOME to an empty scratch dir):

- probe_session_format classifies at least 320 of the ~323 files under

- Session rows for omp session ids number at least 300, not 16.
- No omp record carries a surrogate `nouuid_...` uuid.
- parent_uuid is non-null for at least 85% of omp records.
- No `title` preamble line is inserted as a record, and no `title` preamble

There is no equivalence executor -- "equivalence" and "round_trip" are
declarable but raise. So the invariance claim must be ENCODED as signed flows
over a closed system, and the encoding must make an unequal pair of readings
impossible to cancel by accident.

Encode it as a multiset-fingerprint conservation, which is exactly that:

  For reading A (header at line 0) and reading B (same transcript with the

      w(t) * (count_A(t) - count_B(t))
  Print {"flows": [...]} plus any legibility fields you like.

A surplus of one tuple in A cannot silently cancel a deficit of a different
tuple in B, because the weights differ -- that is the whole point of the
weighting and it is why a flat +1/-1 encoding would be unsound here.

`uv tool install --force .` on 2026-08-06 19:55 resolved mcp 2.0.0, and the
server would not start:

  from mcp.types import AnyUrl, Resource, TextContent, Tool
  ImportError: cannot import name 'AnyUrl' from 'mcp.types'

systemd restarted it four times and it failed identically each time
(journalctl --user -u ingest-sessions). The MCP server was down until the
import was fixed.

Cause: AnyUrl is a pydantic type. mcp re-exported it from mcp.types through
1.x and dropped that re-export in 2.0.0. pyproject declares `mcp>=1.0` with no
upper bound, so any fresh resolve picks 2.x and breaks the import. pydantic was
never a declared dependency either -- the import rode in transitively through
mcp.

Fixed by importing AnyUrl from pydantic (its actual home) and declaring
`pydantic>=2` as a direct dependency, so the mcp pin stays open and the import
no longer depends on another package's re-export surface.

This is recorded rather than dispatched: it was an active outage found while
verifying is-5a7 against the live server, and the fix is a one-line import
correction plus the dependency declaration it implies. Verified by restarting
the service and confirming it reached active (running) and answered a query.

CLOSED 2026-08-06. omp session transcripts are ingested into the live corpus.
Delivered as four leaves, each spec-derived and graded through the reducer:

  is-5a7.1  omp format adapter (src/ingest_sessions/omp.py)        merged_ff
  is-5a7.2  one recursive discovery function over a root list      merged_ff
  is-5a7.3  route each discovered file to its adapter (claude|omp) merged_ff
  is-5a7.4  header is at line 1, not line 0 (bounded scan)         merged_ff, 12/12

.1 and .2 alone did not add up to a feature: nothing called the adapter, which
is what .3 wired. .4 came out of rehearsal against the real corpus -- the
pebble text (and omp's own docs) said the session header is line 0, but on
disk 307 of 323 files carry a rewritten-in-place {"type":"title",...,"pad":...}
line first and the header at line 1, so probe_session_format sent them down
the Claude path. Measured before the fix: 201 records, 16 session rows.

MEASURED ON THE LIVE CORPUS after `uv tool install --force .` and
`systemctl --user restart ingest-sessions` (query via the running MCP server):

  file_mtimes by corpus
    [{"corpus": "claude", "files": 7822}, {"corpus": "omp", "files": 333}]
    on disk: 3866 claude, 340 omp. The 7 omp files not yet recorded are newer
    than the cold scan and are the watchdog's; omp_records has been climbing
    on its own (94,087 -> 94,836) while these measurements ran, which is that
    watchdog routing omp live.

  omp records / parent linkage / surrogate uuids
    [{"omp_records": 94087, "parented": 93754, "parent_rate": 0.9965,
      "surrogate_uuid": 0}]
    claude, for comparison
    [{"claude_records": 1354099, "parented": 1240906, "parent_rate": 0.9164}]
    Baseline through the unmodified Claude parser was 92,013 records, 100%
    surrogate uuid, 0% parented, zero user/assistant rows.

  omp session rows / first_prompt
    [{"omp_session_rows": 334, "with_first_prompt": 332, "null_first_prompt": 2}]
    e.g. 019fcc80-5507-7000-9ea6-dd9f58263b25 -> "which user are you
    authenticated as?" (6863 messages)

  session_id provenance -- header id, never the filename stem
    340 of 340 files have a stem that differs from their header id; 286 are
    subagent files named after an agent LABEL.
    AcceptanceCriteriaCheckboxes.jsonl ->
      {"header_id": "019f4d4e-0cd3-7000-8827-7369e8ec9942",
       "records_under_header_id": 336,
       "filename_stem": "AcceptanceCriteriaCheckboxes",
       "records_under_filename_stem": 0}

  omp record type histogram (top): custom 31184, toolResult 30917,
  assistant 29387, user 1756, model_change 370, session_init 284,
  thinking_level_change 189, ttsr_injection 52, compaction 23 -- the
  SessionEntry union typed as itself, with chat turns typed by role.

  get_session on an omp subagent session returns 336 records threaded by
  parentId (first record parent null, second parented to it).

REHEARSED FIRST against a throwaway DuckDB (/tmp/rehearse_omp3.duckdb), never
the live corpus: 330 omp files, 92,892 records, 99.65% parented, 0 surrogates,
330 session rows / 328 with first_prompt, alongside 25 Claude files ingested
in the same pass to prove the router still sends those down the Claude path.

STILL RUNNING, unattended: the embed+FTS sweep over the 94k new omp records
(server-side `sync`, 1,280 done at close). Ingestion, `query` and
`get_session` cover omp now; `retrieve_relevant`'s vector and BM25 arms cover
it once that sweep finishes. It is CPU-only (see is-af8) and the server
re-runs it on its own interval, so it needs no operator action.

Found and fixed on the way: is-19e (P0) -- reinstalling resolved mcp 2.0.0
under the open `mcp>=1.0` bound, which dropped `mcp.types.AnyUrl` and the 1.x
`Server` decorator API, and the service crash-looped. Pinned `mcp<2`, moved
the AnyUrl import to pydantic and declared pydantic directly.

Resolved in place 2026-08-06, before is-5a7.3 landed. The frozen floor
`claude_paths_recorded >= 7779` in derived-is-5a7.3.spec.json c5 was replaced
by two assertions that grade the change rather than the retention job:

  claude_paths_on_disk_count                     ge 100
  claude_paths_on_disk_missing_from_file_mtimes  eq 0

Exact coverage of whatever is on disk at scan time is strictly stronger than a
floor -- it cannot be satisfied by a corpus that merely happens to be large --
and it cannot be moved by Claude Code's session-retention cleanup, which is
what falsified the original number (~/.claude/.last-cleanup 2026-08-06T15:50:45.747Z,
7,780 *.jsonl -> 3,844).

A second correction followed on the same clause (9589267): the first fix passed
VACUOUSLY under grading, reporting omp_paths_recorded=0 and
claude_paths_..._missing=0 together, because spec_oracle's hermetic child env
(_construct_oracle_child_env) pins HOME to a fresh empty scratch dir, so an
oracle resolving the roots via Path.home() saw two empty directories. c5 now
requires the probe to resolve the real roots from pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir,
and the >= 100 floor makes empty roots fail loudly instead of passing silently.
Product code still uses Path.home(), which is correct for the server.

Commits: 70a3241, 9589267 (spec), 8fee661 (oracle). is-5a7.3 then graded green
and merged_ff.

service stopped, because the single DB thread was saturated (is-189/is-cea

and DuckDB invalidated the database until restart. is-189's 4GB
INGEST_SESSIONS_DB_MEMORY_LIMIT cannot checkpoint this corpus. Raised to 24GB
via a committed-in-place systemd drop-in at
~/.config/systemd/user/ingest-sessions.service.d/10-db-memory.conf, which
